items.title: Eddie Summers Interview, 1963-11-11
items.q: Professor Shining, but the other one around to charge the ball.

ctx.x: Well, uh, he's teaching me about music, but, uh, I see that wasn't, that wasn't a go at that time, was it, Harry? That wasn't a go at that time. The music was okay, but he wanted some of that, uh, rough stuff. Yeah. How much did he charge for lessons? Do you remember that? Well, he used to charge me cheaper. He'd charge me a dollar quarter. That was for an hour, or what? No, a dollar quarter for about two hours. We was kind of friends, like. Yeah. We was friends, like. Uh-huh. How much did he charge everybody? I…

I guess lessons were pretty cheap in those days. Lessons were cheap anyway, though, you know? Well, I mean, I have it one charge dollar, dollar, dollar. Yeah. Professor Shining, but the other one around to charge the ball. Quiet. Yeah. And he'd give you a lesson to him. Yeah. I'm telling you. Let me think, uh, where did we get to, uh, in the 40s, uh, what, what, uh, so you just went back with, uh, Sheik's band when you came back here from California?
When I came back from California. When I went back with Sheik. Uh-huh. When I played different job, spot job with other bands. Yeah.
